description: A sine body and a bandpassed noise, each with its own envelope, crossfaded and saturated, built from the 808 and 909 snares

params.text: Sets the resting frequency of the sine body, 160Hz to 360Hz
Sets how fast the pitch envelope falls, 5ms to 35ms; the tooltip and the manual say the top is 25ms
Sets how far the pitch envelope lifts the body at the start of a hit, up to 500Hz, and how far it lifts the noise filter, up to 5000Hz
Sets the centre of the bandpass filter on the noise, 1000Hz to 6000Hz; the tooltip and the manual say the top is 5000Hz
Sets how fast the noise fades, 5ms to 80ms
Sets how fast the sine body fades, 5ms to 55ms; the tooltip and the manual say the top is 50ms
Crossfades the two sources: fully anticlockwise gives the sine body alone and fully clockwise the noise alone
Sets how far SATURATION can go: L multiplies by up to 3, M by up to 11, H by up to 101; the switch's own tooltip reads 2x, 10x and 100x, which is the part added to 1
Multiplies the mix before the output clips at 5V, from 1 fully anticlockwise to the ceiling the L | M | H switch sets
Fires the snare; a rising edge at the trigger jack does it too

inputs.text: A rising edge above 0.5V fires the sound; the length of the gate makes no difference
Adds to the PITCH DECAY knob
Adds to the PITCH ENV AMT knob
Adds to the NOISE COLOR knob
Adds to the NOISE DECAY knob
Adds to the BODY DECAY knob

notes: a CV input is bipolar and is added to its knob: 10V there is worth the knob's whole travel, -10V cancels a knob that is fully up, and the total is clamped to the knob's own range
the mix is doubled after the saturation multiplier, so even at the lowest setting a loud hit reaches the 5V clip
the pitch envelope drives the noise filter as well as the body, which is why turning PITCH ENV AMT up brightens the snap and not only the thump
